title: Because, So and But
description: Join your sentences the way Gulf speakers do: a reason with لأن, a purpose with عشان, a consequence with عشان كذا, a concession with مع إن — and the polite art of the excuse, where 'the circumstances' is a complete explanation.
approach: Authentic video with scaffolding — excuses and explanations from skits and vlogs, paused at every connector, then a role-play where you arrive late and talk your way out of it.
unlock_condition: Give a reason, a purpose and a consequence in three joined sentences; ≥8/10 on the connector quiz
can_do: Give a reason and a consequence
Join sentences with but, although, in order to
Make an excuse politely and accept one

grammar.title: لأن، عشان، عشان كذا: reason, purpose, result
grammar.explanation: Three words do most of the joining in Gulf speech. لأن (because) comes before a full sentence and usually takes a pronoun ending: لأني تعبان (because I'm tired), لأنه مسافر (because he's away). عشان does two jobs: before a noun it is 'because of' (عشان الزحمة — because of the traffic) and before a present verb it is 'so that / in order to' (عشان أوصل بدري — so I arrive early). Turn the result around with عشان كذا (that's why): الزحمة كانت مرة، عشان كذا تأخرت. Kuwaitis and Emiratis say عشان جذي / عشان جي for the same thing. None of these change the word order — the sentence after them is a normal sentence.

examples.english: I didn't come because I was tired
I left early because of the traffic
I study in order to pass

examples.arabic: السيارة خربانة، عشان كذا جيت تكسي
examples.transliteration: is-sayyaara kharbaana, ʿashaan kidha jayt taksi
examples.english: The car is broken, that's why I came by taxi

grammar.title: بس، لكن، مع إن: but and although
grammar.explanation: The everyday 'but' is بس, which you already use for 'only' and 'enough' — حلو بس غالي (nice but expensive). لكن is the same 'but' with a slightly more careful tone, common when someone is explaining themselves. For 'although' the Gulf uses مع إن plus a sentence: مع إني تعبان، جيت (although I'm tired, I came). Like لأن, مع إن usually carries a pronoun ending — مع إنه، مع إنها. Trap: كمان and برضو are Egyptian; the Gulf says بعد for 'also'.

examples.arabic: أبي أجي بس ما عندي سيارة
examples.transliteration: abi aji bas ma ʿindi sayyaara
examples.english: I want to come but I have no car
Although it was expensive, I bought it

culture.title: The reason offered is often not the reason
culture.note: Lateness is normal and rarely apologised for at length; a one-word explanation — الزحمة، الظروف، كان عندي مشوار — is a complete excuse, and the polite listener accepts it with ما عليه or ولا يهمك without asking for detail. Saying 'the circumstances' (الظروف) is not evasive: it tells the other person you do not want to go into it, and they will not. Pushing for the real reason costs both of you face. When you are the one late, lead with والله and the reason, then move on quickly; a long apology makes people uncomfortable.

phrases.english: Never mind, what matters is you came
God forgive you, you kept us waiting

vocabulary.teaching_note: Takes a pronoun ending before a pronoun subject: لأني، لأنك، لأنه، لأنها، لأنهم. Before a noun it stands alone: لأن الطريق مقفل. Written online as لان / لانه.
vocabulary.image_scene: A woman pointing at a flat tyre on her car, a speech bubble with an arrow from the tyre to her watch.

example.english: I didn't go because the car is broken

vocabulary.video_hint: Someone explaining themselves: ليش…؟ — لأن… ; skit characters justifying lateness.

vocabulary.english: so that / in order to / because of
vocabulary.teaching_note: Before a verb it is 'so that' (عشان أوصل بدري); before a noun it is 'because of' (عشان الزحمة); before a person it is 'for the sake of' (عشانك — for you). Saudis also say علشان. The single most useful connector in the dialect.
vocabulary.image_scene: An alarm clock set early on a bedside table, a suitcase by the door with a plane ticket on it.

example.arabic: قمت بدري عشان أوصل قبل الزحمة
example.transliteration: gimt badri ʿashaan awṣal gabl iz-zaḥma
example.english: I got up early so I'd arrive before the traffic

vocabulary.video_hint: عشان between an action and its purpose in vlog narration; عشانك in warm exchanges.

vocabulary.teaching_note: Literally 'because of this'. Saudi كذا, Kuwaiti جذي, Emirati جي — same phrase, three pronunciations. Trap: كده is Egyptian and will not be understood as Gulf; لذلك is for writing.
vocabulary.image_scene: Domino tiles falling in a line, the last one knocking a cup off a table.

example.arabic: كان مريض، عشان كذا ما جا
example.transliteration: kaan mariiḍ, ʿashaan kidha ma ja
example.english: He was ill, that's why he didn't come

vocabulary.video_hint: A conclusion drawn on camera: عشان كذا / عشان جذي before the result.

vocabulary.teaching_note: Two words that behave like لأن: they take a pronoun ending (مع إني، مع إنه). The main sentence can come first or second. Trap: رغم أن is MSA; بالرغم is heard but bookish.
vocabulary.image_scene: A man in a raincoat walking through heavy rain toward a football pitch, ball under his arm.

example.english: Although the weather was hot, we went out

vocabulary.video_hint: A speaker conceding a point: مع إنه… بس…

vocabulary.teaching_note: The careful 'but'. بس does the same job in casual talk; لكن appears when someone is explaining or objecting a little more formally, and it is how 'however' comes out in speech. Never و لكن with a pause — say it as one word.
vocabulary.image_scene: A woman holding up one finger in a 'but wait' gesture while looking at a menu.

example.english: The restaurant is nice, but a bit expensive

vocabulary.video_hint: Review and opinion clips: praise, then لكن, then the drawback.

vocabulary.teaching_note: The noun behind 'because'. وش السبب؟ (what's the reason?), بدون سبب (for no reason), بسبب (because of). Plural أسباب.
vocabulary.image_scene: A magnifying glass over a question mark, an arrow leading to a light bulb.

example.english: What's the reason? Why didn't you come?

vocabulary.video_hint: Someone asking for an explanation: وش السبب / شنو السبب؟

vocabulary.teaching_note: Note the Gulf vowel pattern ʿudhur, two syllables. عندي عذر (I have an excuse), بدون عذر, and the formal apology اعذرني (excuse me / forgive me). Plural أعذار — used to tease someone who always has one.
vocabulary.image_scene: A schoolboy holding out a crumpled note to a teacher, one hand behind his back with fingers crossed.

example.english: Do you have an excuse or not?

vocabulary.video_hint: Comedy about excuses: أعذار الموظفين, a boss asking وش عذرك؟

vocabulary.teaching_note: The universal, no-questions-asked excuse: الظروف (the circumstances) or ظروف خاصة (private circumstances). Singular ظرف. Saying it closes the topic politely; hearing it means do not ask.
vocabulary.image_scene: A man shrugging with palms up beside a closed calendar page and a phone with many missed notifications.
vocabulary.video_hint: الظروف offered as an explanation and accepted without follow-up.

vocabulary.teaching_note: The gracious reply to any excuse or apology: literally 'nothing on it'. Also معليش, and the warmer ولا يهمك (don't let it bother you). Saying عادي (normal) does the same job among friends.
vocabulary.image_scene: A host waving a hand kindly at a guest arriving at the door with an apologetic face.

example.english: Never mind, come and sit down

vocabulary.video_hint: An apology being waved away with ما عليه / ولا يهمك.

vocabulary.teaching_note: A participle: متأخر، متأخرة، متأخرين. Works for people (ليش متأخر؟) and times (الساعة متأخرة). The verb is تأخر (to be late). Opposite: بدري (early).
vocabulary.image_scene: A man running toward an office building glancing at his watch, the sun already high.
vocabulary.video_hint: Someone arriving late and being asked ليش متأخر؟ — skits about the office.

vocabulary.teaching_note: Both traffic jams and crowded places (المول زحمة). The Gulf's most common excuse and the most common complaint. Also زحمة مرة / زحمة وايد for 'really busy'.
vocabulary.image_scene: A wide highway at dusk packed with white SUVs, brake lights all the way to the horizon.

example.english: The road has been jammed since morning

vocabulary.video_hint: Dashboard shots of a jam with الزحمة in the narration; complaints about الرياض or دبي traffic.

vocabulary.teaching_note: Literally 'by God', but in speech it simply means 'honestly' and starts half the excuses and stories in the Gulf. Stronger: والله العظيم. As a question — والله؟ — it means 'really?'. Do not overuse it in serious promises; there it is a real oath.
vocabulary.image_scene: A young man with a hand on his chest and an earnest face, talking to a friend.
vocabulary.video_hint: والله opening an explanation or answering a doubt: والله؟ — والله.

vocabulary.teaching_note: The classic Gulf excuse: كان عندي مشوار (I had an errand) needs no further detail. Also a car ride or outing: مشوار قصير. Plural مشاوير — عندي مشاوير means a busy day of running around.
vocabulary.image_scene: A car key and a shopping list on a kitchen counter, the front door open behind them.
vocabulary.video_hint: Someone leaving with عندي مشوار; vlogs titled مشاوير اليوم.

vocabulary.teaching_note: 'Reason' with بـ in front: بسبب الزحمة (because of the traffic). Takes a noun or a pronoun ending — بسببك (because of you) can be an accusation or thanks depending on tone. عشان does the same job more casually.
vocabulary.image_scene: A cancelled-flight board at an airport with a dust storm visible through the windows.

example.english: The flight was delayed because of the dust

vocabulary.video_hint: News-style explanations in vlogs: بسبب الجو، بسبب الزحمة.

vocabulary.teaching_note: A word Gulf speakers cannot argue without: ما كنت بأجي أصلاً (I wasn't going to come anyway), هو أصلاً ما يعرف (he doesn't even know). Sits at the end or the middle of the sentence. Written اصلا online.
vocabulary.image_scene: A woman shrugging with a half-smile, an unopened invitation card on the table in front of her.

example.english: I wasn't going to come anyway

vocabulary.video_hint: أصلاً dropped into an argument or a dismissive reply in skits.

vocabulary.teaching_note: The verb form of متأخر: تأخرت (I was late), تأخر الباص (the bus was late), لا تتأخر (don't be late). The initial hamza is barely heard: tʾakhkhar.
vocabulary.image_scene: A bus stop with two people checking their phones, an empty road stretching away.

example.english: I was late because of the traffic

vocabulary.video_hint: تأخرت as the first word of an apology; لا تتأخر at a goodbye.

vocabulary.teaching_note: The soft apology for a slip: ما قصدت (I didn't mean it), ما كان قصدي (it wasn't my intention). From قصد (intention). Pair it with والله for sincerity.
vocabulary.image_scene: A boy holding a broken toy with wide guilty eyes, his sister frowning beside him.

example.english: Sorry, honestly I didn't mean to

vocabulary.video_hint: An apology after a misunderstanding: ما قصدت / مو قصدي in skits.

vocabulary.teaching_note: Said with a smile to someone who let you down a little — the Gulf way of forgiving and telling off in one breath. To a woman الله يسامحج / يسامحك. The reply is usually a laugh or والله ما قصدت.
vocabulary.image_scene: An older woman wagging a finger at a grinning young man carrying late shopping bags.

example.english: God forgive you, you kept us waiting

vocabulary.video_hint: A relative half-scolding a latecomer with الله يسامحك.

dialogue.speaker: Haya
dialogue.arabic: والله الزحمة كانت مرة، وكان عندي مشوار قبل
dialogue.transliteration: wallah iz-zaḥma kaanat marra, w-kaan ʿindi mishwaar gabl
dialogue.english: Honestly, the traffic was terrible, and I had an errand before.

dialogue.speaker: Noura
dialogue.arabic: ما عليه. بس ليش ما اتصلتي؟
dialogue.transliteration: ma ʿalayh. bas laysh ma ittaṣalti?
dialogue.english: Never mind. But why didn't you call?

dialogue.speaker: Haya
dialogue.arabic: لأن الجوال ما فيه شحن، عشان كذا ما قدرت
dialogue.transliteration: liʾann il-jawwaal ma fiih shaḥan, ʿashaan kidha ma gidart
dialogue.english: Because the phone had no charge, that's why I couldn't.

dialogue.speaker: Noura
dialogue.arabic: الله يسامحك. مع إنك متأخرة، الأكل بعده حار
dialogue.transliteration: allah ysaamḥich. maʿ innich mitʾakhkhra, il-akil baʿdah ḥaarr
dialogue.english: God forgive you. Even though you're late, the food is still hot.

dialogue.speaker: Haya
dialogue.arabic: ما قصدت أتأخر، والله. يالله نتغدى
dialogue.transliteration: ma gaṣadt atʾakhkhar, wallah. yalla nitghadda
dialogue.english: I didn't mean to be late, honestly. Come on, let's have lunch.

sound_spotlight.explanation: The hamza is swallowed and the doubled n carries the stress: li-AN-ni. Learners who say it as three separate pieces sound like a textbook; hear it as one word.
Saudi kidha, Kuwaiti chidhi, Emirati chee — the same 'this way'. The ك turns into ch east of Saudi; you will meet this sound change again in شلونج.
Gulf pronounces ظ and ض the same — a heavy dh made with the tongue pressed low. The u after it is dark, almost like 'oo' in 'door'.

lesson_sequence.detail: A 45-second skit: someone arrives late and explains. Watch once; answer 'was the excuse accepted?'.
Eighteen words with audio and example sentences; the five connectors are colour-coded by job (reason / purpose / result / but / although).
Second viewing with pauses before each connector; tap the one that fits, then hear the line.
Match sentence halves: ما جيت … / … لأني تعبان. Twelve pairs mixing لأن، عشان، عشان كذا، بس، مع إن.
Prompt: you are 30 minutes late to a friend's lunch. Record a three-sentence excuse with والله, a reason and a purpose. Rubric checks the connectors.
Hear five excuses; reply out loud with ما عليه or الله يسامحك and the right tone. Native model plays after each.
Word counter rolls up. Nudge: the next time you are late, say why in Arabic — one sentence is enough.

real_world_prompts.prompt: Think of the last thing you cancelled. Explain it in two sentences: ما قدرت أجي لأن… عشان كذا…
real_world_prompts.context: Shown on the lesson-complete screen. Activates لأن and عشان كذا with the learner's own content.

real_world_prompts.prompt: Listen for عشان today — in a clip, a song or a tutor's speech — and decide each time: because of, or in order to?
real_world_prompts.context: Next-day notification. Receptive noticing of the double role of عشان.

real_world_prompts.prompt: Tell your tutor one thing you like and one drawback, joined with بس or لكن, then add a مع إن sentence.
real_world_prompts.context: Tutor-session card. Contrast connectors in a real exchange.

video_needs.scene: A skit or vlog where someone explains why they were late or absent: the excuse, the connector, and the other person's ما عليه or الله يسامحك.
